newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores to make new proposal to Cosipa.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores to make new proposal to Cosipa.

text.p: Brazilian stevedores were due to make a new proposal to steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to resolve a labor dispute at the company's private terminal at Santos port, an official said.

"The proposal we made on Tuesday was just for bulk products, today we will talk about other products," said Antonio Pinho, second-secretary of the Santos Stevedores' Union. "We are still elaborating the proposal."

Unions representing stevedores, as well as workers who register loading and unloading and cargo controllers, will hold fresh talks with Cosipa officials at 1400 local/1700 GMT, the second round of negotiations since at strike ended last week.
The workers have held two strikes and occupied vessels at the Cosipa terminal in protest against the firm's decision to use its own workers to load and unload vessels.
Stevedores Tuesday proposed to cut their work teams by 40 percent and reduce the number of overtime hours they were eligible for, as far as the loading of bulk products were concerned.

Cosipa handles coal and mineral products in bulk, said a spokeswoman for the port authority. Today's talks were likely to center on the company's exports of steel products and handling of containers for third parties, she added.
Cosipa declined to say who would be taking part in the talks and what the agenda would be.
Earlier this week, it said loading registrars and cargo controllers were due to present their proposals today after failing to bring anything to the first round of talks.
The unions have said they will continue to negotiate until April 30 but warned they could start a fresh strike as of May 1 if no solution had been found by then.
